SeverityFix before orderingWhat to do
critical26 resistor(s) over their derated power
C9, C10, C11, C15, C17, C18, C19, C20, C21, C22		Use a larger package/higher rating, or a higher resistance.
majorNo fiducials on the top side (40 SMD parts)
Add 2-3 fiducials in opposite corners of the top side, or confirm that the panel rails carry them.
majorNo fiducials on the bottom side (103 SMD parts)
Add 2-3 fiducials in opposite corners of the bottom side, or confirm that the panel rails carry them.
major13 via(s) inside SMD pads
C13, C39, C42, C51, C52, C70, L5, R15, R23, R36		Move vias next to the pad (dog-bone) or order filled & capped vias (IPC-4761 type VII).
major7 MLCC(s) within 3.0 mm of the board edge
C1, C8, C35, C39, C40, C41, C63		Move MLCCs >= 3.0 mm from edges and V-score lines, orient them parallel to the edge, or use soft-termination / flexible-termination parts.
major18 IC power net(s) lack a nearby decoupling capacitor
U1, U2, U3, U4, U5, U6, U12, U13, U14, U15		Place a 100 nF capacitor within 5 mm of every power pin (plus bulk capacitance per rail).
majorNo supply net identified for powered tests
Set supply.net (and supply.voltage) in pcbtestkit.json.

1 · Build the test fixture

Fixture PCB with pogo pins (render of the generated .kicad_pcb)
Probe points on the board (red = supply, dark = GND, green = measured)

Parts

  • 34 x pogo pin P75 (32 crown tip, 2 spear tip)
  • 34 x receptacle R75 (fixture drill 1.40 mm)
  • 0805 resistors: 1 x 1800 ohm, 3 x 8200 ohm, 4 x 10000 ohm, 28 x 82000 ohm, 28 x 100000 ohm
  • 1 x pin header 2 x 19, 2.54 mm; 1 x 2-pin 5.08 mm terminal block
  • guide pins matching the board's mounting holes; 4 x M3 standoffs
1
video-fixture.kicad_pcb: Routed by PCB TestKit (134 connections, 128 vias, KiCad's default rules): open it in KiCad, run DRC and order it.
2
Press the receptacles into the plated holes and solder them; insert the pogo pins (crown tips on through-hole leads, spear tips on flat pads - see the probes CSV).
3
Fit the guide pins in the GUIDE holes; they locate the board through its mounting holes. Mount the fixture on M3 standoffs.
4
Solder the divider resistors, header and power terminal. Wire the header to the measurement hardware as shown below.

Wiring

2 · Run a production test

Lower the board onto the guide pins: a pogo pin stands under every test point...
...and press it down: every pogo pin touches its test point
1
Copy the runner folder to the Raspberry Pi and describe your wiring in hardware.json.
2
Once, with known-good boards: python3 pcbtest_runner.py learn --units 3 to fill in signal limits.
3
For every board: place it, press down, run python3 pcbtest_runner.py test --loop and enter the serial number.
4
Green PASS: next board. Red FAIL: the failed checks are listed and stored in results/results.csv.
StepWhat is checked
S1 Visual inspectionPolarity/orientation correct, IC pin-1 orientation matches silkscreen, Through-hole joints filled, leads clipped <= 1.5 mm, No solder bridges on fine-pitch parts, No cracked MLCCs near the board edge
S2 Unpowered short check (rails to GND)+3.3V 100.0.., +5F 100.0.., +5V 100.0.., VAA 100.0..
S4 Rail voltages+3.3V 3.135..3.465, +5F None..None, +5V 4.75..5.25, VAA None..None
S5 Signal levels (idle)BLANK- None..None, EA1 None..None, EA2 None..None, EA3 None..None, EA4 None..None, EA5 None..None

3 · Hand-solder with the jigs

Build order

PassWhatJig
1reflow the 38 SMD part(s) on the top side
2reflow the 102 SMD part(s) on the bottom sidepaste-print nest
3hand-solder C49, C50, CV1, D1, D2, D3, D4, D6, L6, P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P8, P9, P10, P11, P12, RR1, RR2, RR3, RR4, RR5, RR6, RR7, RR8, U1, U8, U9, U12, U13, U14, U15, U16, U17, U18, U19, U21, W5, X1, X2, X3, W4 (top side)jig set

Paste-print nest for the bottom side (pass 2)

The bottom side is printed after the other side has been reflowed. Print video-paste-nest-bottom.stl, put the PCB in it bottom side up: its parts on the underside sit in pockets, the board lies flat and the frame around it is flush with the board, so the stencil lies flat for printing the paste. PLA or PETG: the nest does not go into the reflow oven.

Paste-print nest (342.25 x 136.75 x 8.18 mm)

Top-side parts

3D-printed jig (322.75 x 187.5 x 17.8 mm)
place part hereclearance for assembled partsalignment post

Print video-jig.stl as it is (pockets face up, no supports): PLA or PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 3 walls. The pocket map is the jig as it lies on your desk.

1
Print both jigs as they are (no supports): video-jig-placement.stl (placement jig) and video-jig.stl (holding jig).
The two printed jigs: placement jig (left) and holding jig (right)
2
Put the PCB top side up into the placement jig; the stops around the edge locate it.
3
Fit the hand-soldered parts from above, the normal way: C49 (22pF), C50 (22pF), CV1 (5/30pF), D1 (BAT46), D2 (BAT46), D3 (BAT46), D4 (BAT46), D6 (LED), L6 (470ns), P1 (BNC), P2 (BNC), P3 (BNC), P4 (CONN_2), P5 (CONN_5), P8 (BNC), P9 (CONN_1), P10 (CONN_1), P11 (CONN_1), P12 (CONN_1), RR1 (8x10K), RR2 (8x10K), RR3 (8x10K), RR4 (8x10K), RR5 (8x10K), RR6 (8x10K), RR7 (8x10K), RR8 (8x10K), U1 (24C16), U8 (BT253), U9 (BT473), U12 (SIM4X32), U13 (SIM4X32), U14 (SIM4X32), U15 (SIM4X32), U16 (SIM4X32), U17 (SIM4X32), U18 (SIM4X32), U19 (SIM4X32), U21 (XC1736APD8), W4 (TEST), W5 (TEST), X1 (10MHz), X2 (30MHz), X3 (4.433618MHz). Mind polarity marks. The leads go through their holes into the wells under the board; trim leads longer than 10 mm.
PCB top side up in the placement jig; each part goes straight down into its holes
4
Put the holding jig on top, pockets down: its posts go through the mounting holes and every part sits in its pocket.
The holding jig comes down over the parts, pockets first
5
Hold both jigs together and turn the stack over. Lift off the placement jig: every lead now points up.
Stack turned over, placement jig lifted off: the board lies in the holding jig, leads up
6
Solder all leads from above, clip them, lift the board out with the finger notches.
Solder from above; the jig holds every part flush and square
Placement jig (324.25 x 118.75 x 13.4 mm): lead wells, post holes and locating stops
